scope: WebSocket admission remains reserved until the reader, exactly-once cleanup and connection-owned save/presence work all finish, rather than freeing admission immediately after hub handoff.
Nested connection work extends that same reservation. Rejected work rolls back its reference; a released connection cannot revive it.
Ordinary unregister, slow-peer broadcast retirement and shutdown share one cleanup admission. No change to character locks, durable save/reward journals, timeout clocks or socket-origin policy.

checks.actualTransport: Existing real one-slot WebSocket fixture now keeps an owned task blocked after reader retirement: upgrades still return 503, then ordinary reconnect succeeds when work drains. Invalid-origin reservation recovery remains covered.
checks.inProcess: 64 concurrent work references, exactly-once cleanup, nested task retention, rejected admission rollback, no reservation revival or double release; existing save/reward/ownership/queue regressions also pass.

limits: Bounds retired connection cohorts against the WebSocket gate; not a bound on every task generated by one live connection or independent guild/weekly-raid/PvP completion work. Those admission paths remain separate.

During sealed shutdown, rejected cleanup retains its reservation rather than claiming completion. Independent final journal-all persistence remains authoritative; this is not a durability acknowledgement or automatic database recovery.
Earlier connected production-binary checks predate this change. Latest binary, broader gameplay/load evidence and full 1.72 publication remain unfinished. No player-capacity claim.
